[AHNS (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709) adjusts hardness during training to mitigate false-positive and false-negative effects. Sequential-specific [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) combines uniform warm-up, global candidate recall, and progressively harder stochastic selection. Sampling within a top-M set reduces reliance on a single potentially false negative; it does not establish that unobserved items are truly negative. Its reported backbone experiments do not include NextItNet, so transfer remains a hypothesis.

Sampling correction and hard-negative ranking address different objectives. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) revisits sampled-softmax estimation: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its refined estimator treats these contributions differently and introduces an uncertainty-related weight. For NextItNet, a principled experiment would compare corrected sampling with deliberately hardness-biased training; applying a uniform-proposal correction after top-M mining would misrepresent the actual sampler.

[LLPAUC (WWW 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00844) provides an alternative objective focused on the lower-left ROC region, with theoretical connections to top-K ranking and robustness to noisy feedback. Practical hypotheses: uniform warm-up followed by stochastic hard negatives, exclusion of known training positives, and a separate LLPAUC-loss trial. These can retain one NextItNet model per category. None establishes gains on this benchmark: select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; stronger competitive-negative audit results remain diagnostic evidence.

Closest match: [Preference-Drift-Aware Subsequence Learning (September 2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12556) learns differentiable soft context boundaries from preference-drift signals, pools preference-coherent subsequences, retrieves relevant historical contexts for recent interactions, and gates recent versus global representations. This directly supports learning which historical contexts remain relevant after preference changes. It does not establish that arbitrary suffixes preserve the full history’s target distribution, and its architecture is generative recommendation rather than NextItNet.
